## SETUP, do this first

Base/table are pre-filled on every Airtable node. Just:
1. Workflow 1 must have already filled tab #3 with "Pending Analysis" rows.
2. Click each node and pick its credential from the dropdown: Airtable nodes -> "Airtable Personal Access Token (Lead Gen $0 Framework)"; DataForSEO node -> "DataForSEO API"; Firecrawl node -> "Firecrawl API"; YouTube nodes -> "YouTube Data API Key"; both Gemini Chat Model nodes -> "Google Gemini API".
3. First run: check the DataForSEO/Firecrawl/YouTube response shape in the execution log against the field names used in the "Normalize" nodes, external APIs occasionally rename fields, adjust if needed.

### 1. Get Pending Rows, Loop One at a Time
Reads every "Pending Analysis" row from tab #3 and processes them one business at a time.

nodes.name: Section - 1. Get Pending Rows, Loop One at a Time

parameters.content:
### 2. Reviews + Website (Cheap, Always-On Data)
Last 50 reviews only, plain-text website scrape only, the two cheapest data sources, always fetched.

### 3. Business's Own YouTube Channel
Checks the website text for an embedded channel link first (free); only searches by name as a fallback.

### 4. Gemini Finds the Problem
One business per AI call, never batched, mixing businesses is exactly what breaks accuracy.

### 5. Owner's Channel, Priority Score & Save
Looks up the owner's personal YouTube channel as a bonus, scores priority (problem strength + data completeness), then updates tab #3 and copies weak leads to tab #1.

nodes.name: Section - 5. Owner's Channel, Priority Score & Save

nodes.notes:
PRIMARY and, as of 16 Aug, the ONLY model in use - the Groq fallback is parked (see its note).

Retries restored to 3x20s because there is no longer a fallback to catch a failure. Gemini free-tier 503s are routine here (runs 174, 176, 181, 186).

HARD LIMIT: the free tier allows 20 calls per day. That is the real ceiling on this workflow, not speed. 'Limit Leads This Run' is capped to protect it.

CREDENTIAL: "Google Gemini API".

options.systemMessage:
You are an operations auditor for an automation agency. You examine the public footprint of exactly ONE local business and report EVERY automation opportunity you can find in it, ranked. You are given data for one business only - never mix in evidence from another business.

YOUR CORE QUESTION - THE 500-CLIENT STRESS TEST:
"If 500 new customers contacted this business tomorrow morning, which step of their pipeline would break first?"
Answer that in pipeline_bottleneck, in two or three plain sentences a salesperson could read aloud on a call. Name the step that breaks and what it costs them.

THINK IN PIPES, NOT COMPLAINTS. A business is a pipe carrying cash flow. Most owners try to grow by pouring more water in - more ads, more staff - while the pipe stays clogged downstream by slow responses, manual paperwork and forgotten follow-ups. Your job is to find the clogs. A business with flawless five-star reviews can still be badly clogged, and that is a real, sellable opportunity. NEVER conclude there is no opportunity merely because customers are happy.

REPORT EVERYTHING, NOT JUST THE TOP ONE. Most businesses have two or three genuine opportunities. all_opportunities must list every one you can support, strongest first, one per line, formatted exactly as:
OFFER NAME | Proven or Likely | the specific evidence in one short sentence
Then pick the strongest as the primary for detected_problem, evidence_quote and recommended_offer. A single-line all_opportunities on a business with an obviously thin footprint means you have not looked hard enough.

WHAT MAKES A TASK WORTH AUTOMATING - all three should plausibly hold: it happens daily or weekly, information is copied by hand between forms and software, and delay costs money.

THE OFFER MENU. Use these exact names:
- AI receptionist / WhatsApp bot - unanswered calls, phone as the only real intake route, or nothing capturing enquiries after hours
- Auto-reply and lead capture - enquiries land in a human inbox with no instant acknowledgement, or a form or lead magnet exists with no visible automated response
- Review response automation - reviews unanswered, especially negative ones, or a low owner reply rate
- FAQ bot - the same question recurs across reviews, or the site buries basic answers
- Booking automation - no real self-service booking. TRUST THE MEASURED FOOTPRINT LINE, not your reading of the body text. If booking type is 'Books online instantly', booking EXISTS - never claim it is missing. If it is 'Form, answered by hand', the clog is the manual handling, so recommend AI receptionist or Auto-reply and lead capture instead, not booking automation.
- Scheduling automation - customers report long waits, delays or scheduling friction
- Content system - a channel that is Abandoned, Barely used, showing Few views per video, or Buying views with no real audience. A high view count against a tiny subscriber count means they are renting attention every month instead of accumulating it. A dormant channel means they already invested in video and abandoned it.
- Intake and document automation - downloadable or printable client forms, PDF intake packets, or a separate registration portal all mean staff are re-keying data by hand
- Follow-up and nurture sequence - a lead magnet, blog or heavy social presence generates interest but no email capture exists to hold it
- Database reactivation - a long-established business with a large past-customer base and no visible recall, reminder or win-back system
- Multi-location routing - several locations or phone numbers with no central intake, so enquiries depend on the customer picking the right branch

EVIDENCED VERSUS INFERRED - BE HONEST. Set evidence_type to Proven only when the evidence is counted or directly visible in the footprint or a quote. Otherwise Likely. Score problem_alignment_score: 5 proven by counted or visible evidence, 4 strongly implied by the footprint, 3 a reasonable auditor's inference, 1 to 2 speculative, 0 nothing found. Never invent a fact to raise a score.

CALIBRATION - THIS MATTERS, AND IT HAS BEEN WRONG BEFORE. In past runs, a business that books customers online instantly, with a high owner reply rate and no meaningful complaints, still scored a 5 because one isolated gap was technically findable, such as a single downloadable form on an otherwise well-systemised site. That is miscalibration, not evidence. Award 5 ONLY when the business's overall footprint is thin or actively broken, not when you found one isolated gap on an otherwise strong footprint. A business whose booking type is 'Books online instantly', with an 80%+ review reply rate and no unanswered negative reviews, should score 2 or lower even if some minor automatable task exists, because the pipe is not actually clogged. Award 4 only when the measured footprint makes a real, costly problem hard to explain any other way. Most real businesses land at 3 or below. Before finalizing, ask yourself: would a strong business's minor imperfection and a genuinely struggling business's real problem get the same score from me right now? If yes, you are not discriminating - lower the strong business's score. If every business in a batch scores 4 or 5, re-read the data and mark at least half of them down. NEVER state how long a business has operated unless the measured footprint gives a years-established figure above zero; when it says the site does not state it, say nothing at all about their age.

CLINICAL, ETHICAL AND PRICING COMPLAINTS: complaints about misdiagnosis, unnecessary treatment, upselling, overcharging, rude staff or poor clinical care are NOT fixable by automation. Never recommend an offer that claims to fix them. HOWEVER, if such complaints sit publicly UNANSWERED, that is strong evidence for Review response automation, because the fixable problem is the silence, not the complaint. Describe it as unanswered public criticism damaging their reputation, and never imply the automation addresses the underlying clinical issue.

JUDGE BY MEANING, NOT KEYWORDS. "I rang three times and gave up", "could never get hold of anyone" and "the phone just rings out" are one signal despite sharing no words. Infer the operational failure underneath what the customer describes, including failures the business has not noticed itself. That inference is the entire point of this audit.

evidence_quote goes straight in front of a paying client, so it must read as something a person wrote. Use either an exact quote from a review or the website, or a structural observation written as a complete plain sentence - for example: their site links to downloadable patient forms and a separate registration portal, so someone is re-typing that data by hand. NEVER paste a line from the measured footprint block verbatim. Strings like "Booking on the site: None found" or "Live chat widget: NO" are internal machine output and must never appear in this field. Never fabricate a quote.

Only if the business genuinely shows no automatable clog anywhere should you set the problem fields and all_opportunities to empty strings with problem_alignment_score 0. That should be rare and it is a legitimate answer - some businesses are already well systemised.

owner_name: only extract if visibly signed on a review reply or stated on an About or Team page. Otherwise empty string and confidence 0. Never guess from the business name.

Respond only with the required JSON output.

assignments.name: pipeline_bottleneck
assignments.value: ={{ /too many requests|rate limit|quota|429|exhausted|overloaded|unavailable/i.test(String($json.error || '')) ? 'The AI quota was exhausted on this run, so this lead was left queued as Waiting for analysis and will be picked up automatically on the next run. Every measured fact on this row is still valid.' : 'AI analysis failed on this run for a reason other than quota. The measured facts on this row are still valid. Re-run to get the written analysis.' }}

assignments.name: priority_tier
assignments.value: ={{ (function(){ var o = $('Find Problem and Score').item.json.output; var score = Number(o.problem_alignment_score || 0); var reviews = Number($('Normalize Reviews').item.json.review_count || 0); var fp = $('Assess Digital Footprint').item.json; if (!o.detected_problem || reviews < 10) return 'Not Now'; var wellRun = (fp.booking_type === 'Books online instantly') && Number($('Normalize Reviews').item.json.unanswered_negative_count || 0) === 0; if (wellRun) return score >= 5 ? 'Medium' : 'Not Now'; if (score >= 4) return 'High'; if (score >= 3) return 'Medium'; return 'Not Now'; })() }}

nodes.name: Compute Priority
nodes.notes:
Three tiers. High = solid evidence (score 4+). Medium = a real but weaker finding (score 3). Not Ready = weak evidence, or under 10 reviews.

Override: if OUR OWN measured facts say the business is already well run (real self-service booking AND zero unanswered negative reviews), it is capped at Medium and usually Not Ready, no matter how confident the AI is. This exists because The Dental Group, which is genuinely well systemised, kept scoring High.

Owner reply rate is deliberately NOT used here: it swings between runs (16% then 0% for the same business on 13 Aug) because we only see the newest ~50 reviews, so it must never drive the tier.

nodes.name: Prepare Tab 3 Update
nodes.notes: Pure pass-through convergence point for the success and failure branches. Everything after this reads from THIS node by name, never bare $json, the two Airtable writes further down each reshape $json into an Airtable-record shape, so bare $json would lose these fields after either write.

'Found on their site' : 'None found'; if (prior === 'Found on their site') return 'Found on their site'; if (found.toLowerCase().split('\n').indexOf(existing.toLowerCase()) !== -1) return 'Found on their site'; return 'You added it'; })() }}

nodes.name: Get Latest Upload
nodes.notes: Finds when the channel last posted, which is what separates a dormant channel from an active one. A channel's uploads playlist is always its channel ID with the UC prefix swapped for UU, so this needs no extra lookup call. Fails harmlessly when the business has no channel.

parameters.content:
## 4b. Measure the Digital Footprint

These two steps turn the raw page and channel data into **countable facts** before the AI sees any of it.

**Get Latest Upload** finds when the channel last posted. This is what separates a dormant channel from an active one, identical numbers otherwise, completely different pitch.

**Assess Digital Footprint** reads the site's own links and copy to determine: booking type, downloadable forms, email capture, lead magnet, live chat, location count and years established. This is plain code, not AI, so it gives the same answer every run.

Why it matters: the AI used to guess these from fragmentary page text and got them wrong. It now receives them as measured facts and is told to trust them over its own reading.

nodes.name: Scrape Secondary Page - Firecrawl
nodes.notes: Only runs when Find Secondary Page to Scrape found a Contact/Booking/Forms link, one extra page per business, not a crawl. Same Firecrawl credential as the homepage scrape.

parameters.content:
### 3b. Optional Second Page (Contact / Booking / Forms)
Checks the homepage's own link list for a Contact, Booking, or Forms page. If one exists, fetches it too and merges the text in, most homepages don't publish an email or show real booking type, a dedicated page often does. If none found, this is skipped and costs nothing extra.

nodes.name: Limit Leads This Run
nodes.notes: SAFETY VALVE. Caps how many leads one run analyses. Set to 15 while you are on Google's free Gemini plan (20 AI calls per day). When you move to a paid AI plan, raise this to 1000.

nodes.name: Build Review Batches
nodes.notes: Groups all pending leads into batches of 100 for a single DataForSEO post each. The Airtable record id rides along in the 'tag' field so results can be matched back to the right business.

nodes.name: Post Review Tasks - Batched
nodes.notes:
Posts up to 100 review jobs per call. DataForSEO bills per job, not per API call.

16 Aug: added priority 2 (high) in Build Review Batches. Normal-priority jobs were still 'Task In Queue' after 135s, so 7 of 10 businesses on run 192 were analysed with NO reviews. High priority doubles cost per job (0.00375 -> 0.0075, i.e. ~$7.50 per 1000 leads) and is worth it: reviews are the core evidence.

nodes.name: Wait for All Reviews
nodes.notes: Once for the whole run, no matter how many leads. Raised 90s -> 150s on 16 Aug: at 90s, 8 of 10 DataForSEO jobs were still queued. Combined with priority 2 most jobs should now land on the first collection pass.

nodes.name: List Review Task IDs
nodes.notes: Turns the batched post responses into one item per review job, each carrying its Airtable record id.

nodes.name: Fetch Review Results
nodes.notes: Collecting a finished job is free and fast - DataForSEO only bills the post. No waiting here.

nodes.name: Reviews Ready?
nodes.notes: Splits off any jobs Google had not finished yet. Only those go round for a second look.

nodes.name: Wait for Stragglers
nodes.notes: Second collection pass, once for the whole run, and only for jobs not ready first time. Raised 45s -> 90s on 16 Aug.

nodes.name: Fetch Review Results 2
nodes.notes: Second attempt for the stragglers only.

nodes.name: Combine Review Results
nodes.notes: Joins the first-pass results and the straggler results back into one stream.

nodes.name: Merge Reviews into Records
nodes.notes: Matches each business to its own reviews and works out the counts (negative reviews, unanswered ones, owner reply rate). Produces the exact same fields the old Normalize Reviews node produced, so everything downstream is unchanged.

parameters.content:
## 0. Fetch ALL reviews first, this is the speed fix

**What changed and why.** This whole row used to live *inside* the loop. Every business posted its own review job, then the workflow sat still for 45 seconds, then collected one result. Ten businesses meant ten 45-second naps, 11 minutes of the last 17-minute run spent doing nothing at all.

**Now:** every review job is posted up front in batches of 100, the workflow waits **once**, and all results come back together. The loop then runs with reviews already in hand.

The wait no longer grows with your lead count. 10 leads or 1,000 leads, same 90 seconds.

**Cost is unchanged.** DataForSEO bills per review job, not per API call.

⚠️ **Limit Leads This Run is set to 15.** Deliberate: Google's free Gemini plan allows only 20 AI calls per day. Raise it to 1000 once you are on a paid AI plan.

nodes.name: Section - 0. Fetch ALL Reviews First (Speed Fix)

parameters.content:
## One model: Gemini

Gemini is the only model here. A Groq fallback was built and tested on 16 Aug, then **removed at the operator's instruction** to be revisited later. Everything needed to rebuild it is below.

### Why it was removed
It worked *technically* but failed our own quality bar. On exec 193 it:
- pasted our internal machine wording back as client-facing evidence (*"booking page is listed as unconfirmed"*)
- marked `evidence_type: Proven` while the same finding said `Likely`
- listed 7 of the 11 offers at once
- scored a 5.0-star practice with zero unanswered complaints as **High**

Classic confidently-wrong, the exact failure mode this project keeps hitting.

### To rebuild it
1. Add a **Groq Chat Model** node, credential `Groq API (Lead Gen Prospecting)`.
2. Model **`openai/gpt-oss-120b`**. NOT `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` (HTTP 400, Groq's Llama models reject the strict json_schema this agent needs). NEVER `llama-3.1-8b-instant` (far too small).
3. Connect it to `Find Problem and Score` on **ai_languageModel input 1**.
4. Set `Enable Fallback Model` = true on the agent.
5. Re-test against a lead Gemini already scored and compare tier + evidence quote side by side before trusting it.

⚠️ With no fallback, a spent Gemini allowance re-queues leads as `Waiting for analysis`. Nothing is lost, the next run picks them up.

nodes.name: Reviews Ready After 2nd Pass?
nodes.notes: Anything still queued after two passes gets one final attempt.

nodes.name: Wait for Slow Stragglers
nodes.notes: Third and final collection pass, once for the whole run. Anything still queued after this is genuinely too slow and the lead is analysed without reviews.

nodes.name: Fetch Review Results 3
nodes.notes: Final attempt. Collecting a job is free (cost 0), so extra passes cost nothing but time.
